title: Parenting interventions to promote early child development in the first three years of life: a global systematic review and meta-analysis
quick: Talking, playing and responding to your baby help support development.
detail: Pooled benefits across cognitive, language, motor, emotional and attachment outcomes; responsiveness-focused programs tended to have greater effects for some outcomes.
funding: WHO grant APW-201931623; no funder role declared
financial_ties: Authors declared no competing interests; Harvard academic affiliations. Underlying trial funding not audited.
access: Original PLOS full text funding/COI, abstract and figures
limitations: Varied interventions, outcome instruments and settings; not proof of IQ gains or a prescribed daily dose.

title: Shared Picture Book Reading Interventions for Child Language Development: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
quick: Reading together can help children learn and use words.
detail: Expressive language d=.41, receptive d=.26; caregiver skill d=1.01; intervals not extracted.
funding: Author support: Rhodes Trust, Oppenheimer Memorial Trust, WITS NRF Centre; DECIPHer joint charities/public funders
financial_ties: Full COI not accessible; separate author support from review grant and underlying trial funding
limitations: Not exclusively infants; no exact reading minutes inferred; review membership overlap with P4-01 pending.

title: Association of the Type of Toy Used During Play With the Quantity and Quality of Parent-Infant Communication
quick: Simple toys and books can encourage more talking than electronic toys.
detail: Adult words/minute 39.62 electronic, 55.56 traditional, 66.89 books; conversational turns likewise higher.
funding: American Speech-Language-Hearing Foundation; no funder role declared
financial_ties: No COI reported; Northern Arizona University; coding assistants paid by project.
limitations: Small volunteer sample; immediate speech counts, not long-term language scores; no brand comparison.

title: Early Childhood Screen Use Contexts and Cognitive and Psychosocial Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
quick: What children watch, and whether you watch with them, matters as well as screen time.
detail: Small associations: background TV and program viewing with lower cognitive outcomes; co-use with higher cognitive outcomes. 65 weak, 27 moderate, 8 strong study quality.
funding: Australian Research Council Centre of Excellence for the Digital Child CE200100022
financial_ties: No conflicts reported; center-level partner support beyond article disclosures not checked.
access: Original JAMA results, methods and disclosure
limitations: Observational correlation; considerable heterogeneity; not proof screens directly cause delay, not a license for infant screen use.

title: Associations Between Screen Use and Child Language Skills: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
quick: More screen time was linked with weaker language skills, while shared viewing was linked with stronger skills.
detail: Screen exposure, background TV, educational programs and co-viewing estimates kept separate.
funding: Specific review funding not located in inspected HTML
financial_ties: No COI reported; Christakis journal editor recused from editorial decision
access: Original JAMA article disclosure, indexed abstract
limitations: Not causal; study overlap with P4-04 unverified.

title: Learning-induced neural plasticity of speech processing before birth
quick: Babies can learn some sound patterns before birth.
detail: EEG differences after prenatal speech-like exposure.
funding: Not verified
financial_ties: Not verified
limitations: Brain response is not IQ, vocabulary or long-term benefit; no loud sound device recommendation.

title: Prenatal Music Exposure Induces Long-Term Neural Effects
quick: Babies may recognize sounds they heard before birth. That does not mean music makes them smarter.
detail: Neural responses to familiar melody after birth and at four months.
funding: Academy of Finland, ERANET-NEURON PANS, University of Helsinki graduate grant, Finnish Cultural Foundation
financial_ties: Authors declare no competing interests
access: Indexed original PLOS abstract, funding, COI
limitations: Small sample; related research group to P4-06; cohort independence unverified; no clinical long-term cognition.

title: Maternal choline supplementation during the third trimester of pregnancy improves infant information processing speed: a randomized, double-blind, controlled feeding study
quick: Choline matters, but one small trial does not prove extra choline boosts intelligence.
detail: Higher versus lower total intake group had faster infant processing task performance.
funding: Egg Nutrition Center, Beef Checkoff, US public funding; authors report no funder role; complete exact grant list pending
financial_ties: Industry promotion funding; complete individual disclosures pending primary extraction
access: Primary PubMed indexed grant/disclosure and abstract
limitations: Same cohort as P4-09 and P4-11; small sample, surrogate outcome; not supplement dosing guidance.

title: Prenatal choline supplementation improves child sustained attention: A 7-year follow-up of a randomized controlled feeding trial
quick: A small study suggests a possible attention benefit, but larger independent studies are needed.
detail: Higher total maternal choline intake group performed better on challenging sustained attention task; exact effects pending.
funding: NIFA/USDA Hatch 1007195 and Balchem Corp; trainee NICHD and Egg Nutrition Center award
financial_ties: Authors declared no conflicts in 2022; later protocol discloses Canfield consultant for Balchem, arrangement after original study/funding.
limitations: Same cohort as P4-08; only 20 children; task not global IQ; cannot recommend high dose.

title: Phosphatidylcholine supplementation in pregnant women consuming moderate-choline diets does not enhance infant cognitive function: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
quick: A larger trial did not find a clear infant thinking or memory benefit from extra choline.
detail: Different chemical form, population, time and infant tests from Cornell trial.
funding: Gerber Foundation, NIH grants and Egg Nutrition Center; funders no role per authors
financial_ties: Gerber Foundation affiliation/ultimate funding not inferred; author COI full extraction pending
limitations: Not equivalent protocol; both research programs have nutrition-sector funding; no pooled effect or supplement recommendation.

title: The Effect of Maternal Choline Intake on Offspring Cognition in Adolescence: Protocol for a 14-year Follow-Up of a Randomized Controlled Feeding Trial
quick: Researchers plan to look at later development; this is not a result.
detail: Protocol only; later results not established in this pass.
funding: NIH T32 HD087137, Egg Nutrition Center, Balchem Corporation
financial_ties: RLC consultant for Balchem; authors say original study and funding predate arrangement.
limitations: No efficacy data; no double count; dated later relationship, not retroactive proof of bias.

title: Seven-Year Follow-up of Children Born to Women in a Randomized Trial of Prenatal DHA Supplementation
quick: DHA is an important nutrient, but this trial did not find a clear overall IQ boost from extra DHA.
detail: Full scale IQ adjusted difference 1.30 points (95% CI -0.47 to 3.08); some secondary findings; no global cognition benefit established.
funding: NHMRC grants 349301 and 1048493; Croda Chemicals donated study capsules
financial_ties: Makrides advisory boards Nestlé Nutrition Institute, Fonterra, True Origins; Gould honoraria Nestlé Nutrition Institute; payments to institutions.
limitations: Separate from preterm infant supplementation and preterm birth prevention; follow-up not independent cohort; no dosing change.

title: Effects of Regular Exercise During Pregnancy on Early Childhood Neurodevelopment: The Physical Activity for Mothers Enrolled in Longitudinal Analysis Randomized Controlled Trial
quick: Exercise can help maternal health, but an IQ or development boost is not proven.
detail: No detected effect on assessed development domains at one year.
funding: Not verified
financial_ties: Not verified
limitations: Adherence, attrition, exact effect and sponsor data pending.

title: Neurodevelopmental outcome in 7-year-old children is not affected by exercise during pregnancy: follow up of a multicentre randomised controlled trial
quick: Moderate exercise in this trial was not linked to worse development.
detail: No detected adverse neurodevelopment effect at seven years.
funding: Not verified
financial_ties: Not verified
limitations: Not universal safety or evidence of IQ enhancement; medical eligibility independent.

title: Physical Activity Before and During Pregnancy and Neurodevelopment in Early Childhood
quick: Active mothers had children with some better developmental measures, but that cannot prove exercise caused them.
detail: Higher reported maternal activity associated with early outcomes, particularly motor function.
funding: Not verified
financial_ties: Not verified
limitations: Confounding and self-report; compare randomized findings rather than asserting causal benefit.

title: Association between prenatal maternal anxiety and/or stress and offspring's cognitive functioning: A meta-analysis
quick: Stress deserves support, not blame. A stressful day does not determine your baby's future.
detail: Associations vary by definition, timing and outcome; no individual prediction.
funding: Not verified
financial_ties: Not verified
limitations: Confounding, heterogeneous measures, no randomized exposure; no anxiety-inducing optimization.

title: Effect of integrated responsive stimulation and nutrition interventions in the Lady Health Worker programme in Pakistan on child development, growth, and health outcomes: a cluster-randomised factorial effectiveness trial
quick: Everyday responsive play and communication can help children learn.
detail: Responsive stimulation improved cognitive, language and motor scores; social-emotional at 12 months.
funding: UNICEF
financial_ties: Full individual COI pending
limitations: Specific disadvantaged population and supported program; not generalize exact effects; included in broader reviews potentially.

title: Effects of responsive stimulation and nutrition interventions on children's development and growth at age 4 years in a disadvantaged population in Pakistan: a longitudinal follow-up of a cluster-randomised factorial effectiveness trial
quick: Some early-play program benefits continued into preschool.
detail: Higher cognition, language and motor skills in responsive stimulation groups.
funding: Grand Challenges Canada
financial_ties: Full individual disclosures pending
limitations: Same cohort P4-17; no independent replication; follow-up attrition and effect sizes pending.

title: Tummy Time and Infant Health Outcomes: A Systematic Review
quick: Awake, supervised tummy time helps babies practice moving.
detail: Review examines motor and other outcomes; evidence varies by design.
funding: Not verified
financial_ties: Article disclosure not independently opened; unknown
access: Primary indexed abstract; PDF not used as extraction source
limitations: Awake and supervised only; back to sleep; no prescribed duration derived from review.

title: WHO Motor Development Study: windows of achievement for six gross motor development milestones
quick: Babies learn to sit and walk at different ages.
detail: Six 1st–99th percentile windows; not diagnostic cutoffs.
funding: Primary grants not verified
financial_ties: Not verified
access: Primary abstract and WHO HTML index
limitations: Some babies skip crawling; reference range does not replace referral or corrected age.

title: Infant Walker-Related Injuries in the United States
scope: Children under 15 months treated in US EDs
quick: Wheeled baby walkers can cause injuries and are not needed to learn walking.
detail: Study supports avoidable injury concern even after safety standards.
funding: Grant detail not extracted
financial_ties: Not verified
limitations: Injury surveillance not developmental efficacy; no denominator per use.

title: CDC developmental milestones
quick: Check how your child is learning and moving; ask for help if you are concerned.
detail: General development screening at 9,18,30 months and autism screening at 18,24 months per cited AAP guidance.
funding: CDC educational resource; panel ties not assessed
limitations: Checklists not screening tests or diagnosis; loss of skills or concerns deserve professional evaluation.

title: Young Children Learning Multiple Languages: Parent FAQs
quick: Speaking your family's languages does not cause a language disorder.
detail: Multilingual exposure is compatible with healthy development; assessment must consider all languages.
funding: AAP resource; underlying evidence and panel disclosures not audited
limitations: Not proof of universal cognitive advantage; primary bilingual studies needed.

title: Early neurodevelopment in the offspring of women enrolled in a randomized controlled trial assessing the effectiveness of a nutrition + exercise intervention on the cognitive development of 12-month-olds
quick: Some early findings are promising, but a combined diet and exercise program cannot tell us which part mattered.
detail: Exploratory subgroup with developmental assessments; exact findings pending.
funding: Not verified
financial_ties: Not verified
limitations: Small subset, selection and multiple outcomes; do not treat exercise alone as intervention.
